# Prompt to Market — Design Spec

> **Status:** Draft v1
> **Date:** 2026-07-28
> **Author:** Sebastian (for Your Majesty)

---

## 1. What It Is

Type a product idea → get a complete launch kit. Client-side only. BYOP via Pollinations auth. No backend. No payments.

**Target user:** Indie hackers, solopreneurs, and creators who need a launch kit fast without hiring a designer or copywriter.

**Core value:** One input, 13 outputs — landing page copy, social posts, hero image, logo, and more. All generated by Pollinations API. All downloadable.

---

## 2. User Flow

```
Home page
  → type product idea (e.g. "AI meal planner for gym bros")
  → click "Generate Launch Kit"
  → loading screen (13 API calls, ~30-60s total)
  → Results dashboard
      → browse outputs by category (Copy / Social / Visuals)
      → copy text outputs with one click
      → download image outputs
      → regenerate any individual output
      → download all as zip
```

---

## 3. Authentication (BYOP)

### Flow (Legacy Fragment — Client-Side Only)

Pollinations BYOP lets users authorize your app to spend their own Pollen. The legacy fragment flow works entirely client-side:

```
1. User clicks "Connect Pollinations"
2. Redirect to: https://gen.pollinations.ai/authorize
     ?redirect_uri=https://yourapp.com/callback
     &client_id=pk_yourkey
3. User authorizes on Pollinations
4. Redirect back: https://yourapp.com/callback#api_key=sk_...
5. Extract api_key from URL fragment
6. Store in localStorage
7. Use in Authorization header for all API calls
```

### Implementation

```typescript
// lib/auth.ts
const CLIENT_ID = 'pk_yourkey'; // Your Pollinations App Key
const REDIRECT_URI = `${window.location.origin}/callback`;

export function initiateAuth() {
  const params = new URLSearchParams({
    redirect_uri: REDIRECT_URI,
    client_id: CLIENT_ID,
  });
  window.location.href = `https://gen.pollinations.ai/authorize?${params}`;
}

export function handleCallback(): string | null {
  const fragment = new URLSearchParams(window.location.hash.slice(1));
  const apiKey = fragment.get('api_key');
  if (apiKey) {
    localStorage.setItem('pollinations_api_key', apiKey);
    window.history.replaceState({}, '', window.location.pathname);
  }
  return apiKey;
}

export function getApiKey(): string | null {
  return localStorage.getItem('pollinations_api_key');
}

export function logout() {
  localStorage.removeItem('pollinations_api_key');
}
```

### Fallback: Manual API Key Input

If the auth flow breaks (CORS, Pollinations downtime), users can paste their API key manually:

```
Input field: "Paste your Pollinations API key (sk_...)"
→ validate by calling GET https://gen.pollinations.ai/v1/models
→ store in localStorage if valid
```

### Key Observations

- The legacy fragment flow avoids PKCE and server-side token exchange — works entirely in the browser
- API key is in the URL fragment (after `#`), so it never hits server logs
- Key expires in 7 days by default (user can revoke anytime from Pollinations dashboard)
- No refresh tokens — re-run the auth flow when key expires
- Developer earnings: enable `earningsEnabled: true` on the App Key to earn 25% markup on user spend

## 4. Outputs

### Text Outputs (7)

| # | Output | Constraints | Character Limit |
|---|--------|-------------|-----------------|
| 1 | Positioning statement | One sentence. Product + who it's for + key benefit. | 150 chars |
| 2 | Landing page copy | Headline (<10 words), subhead (<20 words), 3 benefit bullets, CTA button text | ~300 words |
| 3 | Elevator pitch | Problem → solution → differentiation. Conversational, not salesy. | 60 seconds spoken (~150 words) |
| 4 | Instagram caption | Hook in first line. 3-5 line breaks. 5-10 hashtags at end. 2-3 emojis. | 150-2200 chars |
| 5 | Twitter/X post | Punchy. One clear takeaway. No hashtags in body. Optional thread hook. | 280 chars |
| 6 | LinkedIn post | Professional but human. Hook → story/insight → CTA. 3-5 line breaks. | 150-300 words |
| 7 | Founder FAQ | 5 questions: What? Who? Why different? How much? When? | ~400 words |

### Image Outputs (4)

| # | Output | Dimensions | Model | Notes |
|---|--------|------------|-------|-------|
| 8 | Hero image | 1200×630 | flux | Product concept visual. Clean, modern, professional. |
| 9 | Logo variations | 1024×1024 | flux | 3 styles: minimal, bold, playful. Grid layout. |
| 10 | Social post image | 1080×1080 | flux | Instagram-ready. Product + benefit text overlay concept. |
| 11 | OG image | 1200×630 | flux | Link preview image. Product name + tagline + visual. |

### What's NOT Included (and Why)

| Output | Why Skipped |
|--------|-------------|
| TikTok script | Video scripts need timing, hooks, visual directions. Different workflow entirely. |
| Reddit post | Too contextual — subreddit rules, tone, format vary wildly. Generic Reddit posts are useless. |
| Pricing page | AI can't know margins, market, or willingness to pay. Hallucinated pricing is worse than none. |
| Competitor landscape | AI confidently lists companies that don't exist. Misleading. |
| Pitch deck | Needs real data, traction, team info. AI-generated pitch decks are obvious and harmful. |
| PDF export | YAGNI for v1. Add when users ask. |
| Version history | YAGNI for v1. Regenerate replaces previous output. |

## 5. Prompt Engineering

The system prompts are the product. Each output has a specific prompt that produces consistent, high-quality results.

### 5.1 Positioning Statement

```
System: You are a product positioning expert. Given a product idea, write ONE sentence that captures: what the product is, who it's for, and the key benefit. Be specific, not generic. Avoid buzzwords.

Format: "[Product] is a [category] that helps [audience] [benefit] by [mechanism]."

Example input: "AI meal planner for gym bros"
Example output: "GymPlate is a meal planning app that helps gym enthusiasts hit their protein targets by generating weekly meal plans based on their training schedule and dietary preferences."
```

### 5.2 Landing Page Copy

```
System: You are a conversion copywriter. Given a product idea, write landing page copy with:
- Headline: Under 10 words. Focus on the outcome, not the feature.
- Subhead: Under 20 words. Expand on how the headline's promise is delivered.
- 3 Benefit bullets: Each starts with an action verb. Each ends with a specific outcome. No generic "save time" or "boost productivity" — be concrete.
- CTA button: 2-5 words. Action-oriented. Not "Sign Up" or "Learn More."

Output as JSON:
{
  "headline": "...",
  "subhead": "...",
  "benefits": ["...", "...", "..."],
  "cta": "..."
}
```

### 5.3 Elevator Pitch

```
System: You are a startup pitch coach. Given a product idea, write a 30-second elevator pitch. Structure:
1. Problem (1 sentence): The pain point. Make it relatable.
2. Solution (1-2 sentences): What the product does. Be specific.
3. Differentiation (1 sentence): Why this, not alternatives. Not "we're better" — what's actually different.

Tone: Conversational, not salesy. Like explaining to a friend at a coffee shop. No jargon. No "revolutionary" or "game-changing."
```

### 5.4 Instagram Caption

```
System: You are an Instagram content strategist. Given a product idea, write an Instagram caption that:
- Hook (first line): Stops the scroll. Question, bold claim, or surprising stat.
- Body: 3-5 short paragraphs with line breaks. Tell a story or share a benefit.
- CTA: Tell them what to do next (link in bio, comment, save, share).
- Hashtags: 5-10 relevant hashtags at the end. Mix of broad (#startup) and niche (#mealprep).
- Emojis: 2-3, used sparingly for visual breaks, not decoration.

Constraints:
- First line must work without "see more" truncation (125 chars max)
- No "Hey guys!" or "Hope you're having a great day!"
- No generic hashtags like #love or #instagood
```

### 5.5 Twitter/X Post

```
System: You are a Twitter growth strategist. Given a product idea, write ONE tweet that:
- States a clear benefit or insight
- Is under 280 characters
- Has no hashtags in the body (hashtags tank reach on X)
- Ends with a hook that invites replies or retweets
- Uses simple, direct language

Format: Plain text tweet. No thread. No "🧵" or "1/". Just one tweet.

If the idea is complex, pick the ONE angle that's most tweetable.
```

### 5.6 LinkedIn Post

```
System: You are a LinkedIn content creator. Given a product idea, write a LinkedIn post that:
- Hook (first line): Pattern interrupt. Contrarian take, question, or bold claim. This line shows in the feed preview.
- Body: 3-5 short paragraphs. Share a problem you noticed, how the product solves it, and what you learned.
- CTA: Ask a question or invite comments.
- Tone: Professional but human. Not corporate. Not "I'm thrilled to announce..."
- Format: Short paragraphs (2-3 sentences each). Line breaks between paragraphs. No bullet lists.

Constraints:
- 150-300 words
- No emojis in the first line
- No "🚀" or "💡" or "🔥"
```

### 5.7 Founder FAQ

```
System: You are a startup advisor. Given a product idea, write a Founder FAQ with 5 questions a potential user or investor would ask:

1. "What is [product]?" — One sentence. Clear, jargon-free.
2. "Who is it for?" — Specific audience. Not "everyone."
3. "How is it different from [obvious alternative]?" — Concrete difference, not "we're better."
4. "How much does it cost?" — If pricing isn't decided, say "Pricing is being finalized. Join the waitlist for early access."
5. "When can I use it?" — If no timeline, say "We're building in public. Follow along for updates."

Format as JSON:
{
  "questions": [
    {"question": "...", "answer": "..."},
    ...
  ]
}
```

### 5.8 Image Prompts

```
Hero image prompt:
"Professional product photography of [product concept]. Clean white background. Modern, minimal style. Studio lighting. High quality."

Logo variations prompt:
"Three logo designs for [product name], a [category]. Top: minimal line icon. Middle: bold typographic. Bottom: playful illustrated. White background. Grid layout. Professional branding."

Social post image prompt:
"Instagram post design for [product name]. [Product concept visual]. Clean, modern aesthetic. Subtle gradient background. High quality."

OG image prompt:
"Open graph image for [product name]. [Tagline]. Modern, clean design. 1200x630 aspect ratio. Professional."
```

## 6. Iteration

Each output has controls for regeneration:

| Output Type | Controls |
|-------------|----------|
| Text outputs | "Regenerate" button. Inline edit field → "Regenerate from edit" button. |
| Image outputs | "Regenerate" button only. No image editing (different product). |

### Regenerate Implementation

```typescript
// Each output stores its prompt + user's product idea
// Regenerate = re-call the same API with the same prompt
// Edit = user modifies the text → re-call with modified text as context

async function regenerate(outputId: string) {
  const output = outputs[outputId];
  const result = await callPollinations(output.prompt, output.userInput);
  outputs[outputId] = { ...output, content: result, regeneratedAt: Date.now() };
}

async function regenerateFromEdit(outputId: string, editedText: string) {
  const output = outputs[outputId];
  const prompt = `${output.prompt}\n\nThe user edited the previous output. Here's their version:\n${editedText}\n\nImprove it while keeping their intent.`;
  const result = await callPollinations(prompt, output.userInput);
  outputs[outputId] = { ...output, content: result, regeneratedAt: Date.now() };
}
```

No version history. Previous output is replaced. Add history when users ask for it.

### Pollinations API Client

```typescript
// lib/pollinations.ts
const BASE_URL = 'https://gen.pollinations.ai';

export async function generateText(
  systemPrompt: string,
  userPrompt: string,
  apiKey: string
): Promise<string> {
  const response = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}/v1/chat/completions`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${apiKey}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      model: 'openai',
      messages: [
        { role: 'system', content: systemPrompt },
        { role: 'user', content: userPrompt },
      ],
    }),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    const error = await response.json();
    throw new Error(error.error?.message || 'Text generation failed');
  }

  const data = await response.json();
  return data.choices[0].message.content;
}

export function getImageUrl(prompt: string, width: number, height: number): string {
  const encoded = encodeURIComponent(prompt);
  return `${BASE_URL}/image/${encoded}?model=flux&width=${width}&height=${height}&nologo=true`;
}
```

### Shared Types

```typescript
// lib/types.ts
export interface ProductIdea {
  raw: string; // User's input
  name?: string; // Extracted or generated product name
}

export interface TextOutput {
  id: string;
  type: 'positioning' | 'landing' | 'elevator' | 'instagram' | 'twitter' | 'linkedin' | 'faq';
  content: string;
  prompt: string;
  regeneratedAt?: number;
}

export interface ImageOutput {
  id: string;
  type: 'hero' | 'logo' | 'social' | 'og';
  url: string;
  prompt: string;
  width: number;
  height: number;
  regeneratedAt?: number;
}

export interface LaunchKit {
  idea: ProductIdea;
  texts: TextOutput[];
  images: ImageOutput[];
  createdAt: number;
}
```

## 8. Stitch Usage

Stitch designs all screens. Use `stitch::generate-design` → `stitch::react-components` pipeline.

### Screens to Design

| Screen | Components | Stitch Focus |
|--------|------------|--------------|
| Home | Hero section, input form, feature cards, auth button | Clean, modern, trust-building |
| Results | Output grid, category tabs, download all button | Dashboard layout, card-based |
| TextOutput | Text block, copy button, edit field, regenerate button | Readability, whitespace |
| ImageOutput | Image preview, download button, regenerate button | Image showcase |
| SocialPreview | Instagram/Twitter/LinkedIn mockup frames | Platform-accurate previews |
| LandingPreview | Hero, features, CTA sections | Conversion-optimized layout |
| Loading | Progress indicator, animated dots | Engaging wait experience |
| Callback | Auth success/failure states | Clean transitions |

### Mobile Responsive

All screens must work on mobile. The results dashboard collapses to a single column on mobile. Social previews stack vertically.

## 9. Error Handling

| Error | User Experience | Technical |
|-------|-----------------|-----------|
| API timeout (>60s) | "This is taking longer than usual. Try again?" + retry button | AbortController with 60s timeout |
| Partial failure (some outputs fail) | Show completed outputs. Mark failed ones with error state + retry button. | Promise.allSettled for parallel calls |
| No auth token | "Connect Pollinations to generate your launch kit" + auth button | Redirect to /auth if no key in localStorage |
| Rate limit (429) | "You've generated a lot! Wait a few minutes, then try again." | Parse Retry-After header if present |
| Insufficient pollen (402) | "You're out of Pollen! Top up at enter.pollinations.ai" + link | Link to Pollinations dashboard |
| CORS error | Show manual API key input as fallback | Detect CORS failure, show alternative auth |
| Invalid API key (401) | "Your session expired. Reconnect Pollinations." + auth button | Clear localStorage, re-trigger auth |
| Network error | "Check your connection and try again." + retry button | navigator.onLine check + retry |

---

## 10. Risk Points + Fallbacks

| Risk | Impact | Fallback |
|------|--------|----------|
| Pollinations API blocks client-side CORS | App can't make API calls | Manual API key input field. Server proxy later if needed. |
| Text API hallucinates bad content | Users get useless outputs | Regenerate button. Good system prompts minimize this. |
| Image API slow (>30s per image) | Long wait times | Show text outputs first. Images load async as they complete. |
| Auth flow broken | Users can't connect | Manual API key input. Copy key from enter.pollinations.ai. |
| BYOP fragment flow deprecated | Auth stops working | Migrate to OAuth PKCE with a serverless function (Cloudflare Workers). |
| localStorage quota exceeded | Auth key lost | Single key = ~100 bytes. Won't hit quota. Clear on 401. |
| Pollinations model changes | Prompts produce different quality | Pin model names in prompts. Test periodically. |

---

## 11. What Gets Skipped (YAGNI)

| Feature | When to Add |
|---------|-------------|
| PDF export | When users ask for downloadable one-pagers |
| User accounts / cross-device sync | When localStorage isn't enough (multiple devices) |
| Version history | When users want to compare regenerations |
| Custom prompts / templates | When power users want control over output style |
| Custom domain / white-label | When agencies want to resell |
| TikTok scripts | When the basic version proves the concept |
| Reddit posts | When we can generate subreddit-specific content |
| Pitch deck generation | When we have access to real data APIs |
| Analytics / tracking | When we need to measure conversion |
| Stripe / payments | Never — BYOP only |

## 12. Getting Featured on Pollinations

### Submission

1. Create a Pollinations App Key (pk_...) at enter.pollinations.ai
2. Build and deploy the app
3. Submit via GitHub issue: https://github.com/pollinations/pollinations/issues/new?template=app-submission.yml
4. Category: **Business** (65 apps vs 203 in Image — less competition)
5. Include: name, description, URL, author GitHub handle

### Badges

- **🏅 Pollen (BYOP)** — automatic when using BYOP auth flow
- **🐝 Buzz** — 100+ API requests in 24 hours (traffic-based, automatic)
- **🫧 Fresh** — added in last 30 days (automatic on submission)

### Promotion

- r/SideProject — "I built a tool that generates launch kits from one prompt"
- r/SaaS — target audience lives here
- Indie hacker Twitter — share the tool + a generated example
- Hacker News (Show HN) — if the tool is polished enough

### Why This Gets Featured

- Uses both text AND image APIs in one workflow (most apps use one)
- 11+ API calls per generation (high BYOP usage = Pollinations earns money)
- Novel category — not "another image generator"
- Naturally shareable — people post their generated launch kits
- Targets indie hackers — the most vocal online community
